title: Threads and Atomics
summary: Running C code in parallel - C11 threads with thrd_create and thrd_join, passing arguments and results, data races, mutexes with mtx_lock, atomic variables from stdatomic.h, condition variables, and how POSIX threads and Windows threads map to the same ideas.

cards.q: Why does giving each thread its own result slot avoid locking?
cards.a:
No two threads write the same memory, so there is no data race

Races need two threads touching the same memory with at least one writing. The main thread reads the slots only after `thrd_join`, which orders it after the writes.

cards.q: Why must `cnd_wait` be called in a loop?
cards.a:
A thread can wake without the condition being true, so it must check again

Wake-ups can be spurious, or another thread may have taken the item first. `while (!ready) cnd_wait(&cv, &m);` checks again each time.

cards.q: Several threads only need to increase one shared counter. What is simplest?
cards.a:
an atomic counter with atomic_fetch_add

One atomic operation per increase is indivisible: no lock needed and no updates lost.
